articleTitle: Measurement of multi-path effects in video signals
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The authors set out a quantitative measurement of ghosts (multipath transmission) in a received television waveform. The measurement is based on a non-adaptive technique where the auto-correlation and cross-correlation of the detected video signal and the a priori knowledge of a blank line are used to calculate the relative amplitude and time delay of the ghost. The known ghost is then removed by an IIR digital filter which is also specified. The technique is applicable to PAL, SECAM and NTSC transmissions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated evaluation of colour reproduction for colour video cameras
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: A method to measure and evaluate the performance of a video camera is suggested. The authors discuss such problems as elimination of unwanted effects of electronic circuits, calibration of the measurement system, and how to obtain the matching values for absolute evaluation of colour differences between original and reproduced colours. They also describe a newly developed digital instrument to realize automated evaluation and graphic display of the results of the colour differences.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Objective image impairment detection using image processing
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The evaluation of TV image quality has received much attention in an attempt to ensure optimum picture quality of TV programs. The attention mainly focuses on subjective evaluation of picture quality. The author describes measurements to determine image quality objectively. The quality measurements cover the sharpness of the image, the intensity distribution, colour biases and noise. Algorithms and results for each of these measurements are covered. The measurements were taken with a personal computer fitted with a frame grabber card. As such this picture quality analyzer can be used for quality control on studio outputs, and it can be used as feedback on system defects to allow rapid repair of equipment. It can be used as a technical quality reference that programs have to meet before transmission, instead of the indirect approach to determine technical quality by specifying the format and equipment that outside producers have to use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Facility for subjective evaluation of advanced television in North America
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Canada and the United States hope to introduce an advanced television (ATV) system. However the North American way to attain this objective differs from those adopted in other places in the world. In the United States, the Federal Communication Commission (FCC) plans to establish an ATV standard by 1993. The proposals received were divided into two types: simulcast and NTSC compatible. The Advanced Television Test Center (ATTC) created by the broadcasters, is responsible for the objective tests, as well as for the terrestrial (over-the-air) transmission impairment tests and the production of all the test material recordings. Cable Television Laboratories, created by the National Cable Association, will complete all the tests related to cable impairments. Finally the Advanced Television Evaluation Laboratory in Canada is to complete the subjective assessments with non-expert observers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: In-orbit-testing for DBS satellites
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The term in-orbit-testing (IOT) is used to describe the wide range of tests that are carried out on a satellite after launch. For the purposes of this paper, the meaning of IOT is restricted to the testing of the broadcast payload. It is required for three main purposes: beginning of life testing to ensure that characteristics have not significantly changed during launch and deployment; periodic testing throughout the lifetime of the satellite to confirm that performance remains within specifications, to identify performance trends, and to predict the end of useful life; and investigation of anomalies. The author describes an IOT system designed to test satellites operating on the UK channels of the WARC-BS(77) plan for broadcasting satellites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evolving error performance parameters and objectives for the digital transmission of broadcast television
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The author details the network error performance measurement programme, analysis of the results and methods of testing codec error performance. He points to potential error performance parameters and objectives for digital television transmission and gives useful direction for the aims of equipment in terms of forward error correction (FEC) systems and in-service monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ITC measurement techniques for video and audio performance in independent television in the UK
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The Independent Television Commission (ITC) replaced the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA) for regulatory functions on 1 January 1991. This was one of several changes which have resulted from the UK Broadcasting Act, 1990. The new Broadcasting Act requires the ITC to include conditions in Channel 3, Channel 4 and Channel 5 licences for ensuring high standards for technical quality and reliability. The Technical Regulation Department of the ITC has produced a technical performance code for terrestrial television services. This document is the central reference for high technical standards in television. All major items of broadcasting equipment and defined signal paths are given performance limits for specific tests. There are recommended procedures for all of the video and audio measurements, which provide for standard methods of test procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring programme loudness
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The author briefly looks at the peak programme meter and Vu meter, which have been used for audio level measurements in TV broadcasting. He then discusses the psycho-acoustic aspects of loudness called sensory loudness, Using an engineering model of the ear he develops a practical loudness meter. Finally he looks at automated loudness control;.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RF and IF measurements in TV satellite transmission
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The author details tests to be carried out on television receive only earth stations (TVRO), to ensure that they do not cause excessive electromagnetic interference and are not unduly affected by it. He first looks at intermodulation interference from telecommunication satellites, then looks at emissions from the receiver antenna, receiver housing and receiver power supply. A two-tone-test setup is described to check: conversion oscillator stability; amplification response; amplitude response; intermodulations ratio; and noise figure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MAC: maintenance of practical systems
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: National Transcommunications Ltd (NTL), one of the three successor bodies emerging from IBA UK, own and operate the United Kingdom Direct Broadcast Satellite Uplink. This uplink transmits five D-MAC services to two geostationary satellites situated at 31 degrees West. The equipment at the DBS Uplink is maintained by a mobile maintenance team based in Southampton which is also responsible for the maintenance of approximately seventy television and radio transmitters. The concepts used in the design of the DBS Uplink are based on more than thirty years experience in the construction, operation and maintenance of broadcast transmission systems. The authors describe the equipment installed at the uplink, then discuss the choice of test equipment and give examples of the measurements made.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Test signals and automatic measurement methods for HDMAC signal
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Within the framework of the European HDTV EUREKA-95 project, a new European HDMAC packet transmission standard has been developed, designed to be compatible with the present European D-D2 MAC/Packet transmission standard. The authors propose new compatible test signals and measurement methods for HDMAC. The first part of the paper consists of a brief description of conventional MAC test signals and they deal with HDMAC specificity. The second part is a description of a the new test signals, including the new measurement methods required for HDMAC signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tools for the validation of EUROCRYPT conditional access functions
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The author gives a brief description of the EUROCRYPT access control standard which is used in the France Telecom VISIOPASS D2MAC/Packet television system. A smart card and decoder allow access to encoded TV broadcasts. The author then describes the test equipment which is used to make sure EUROCRYPT systems conform to the standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluating serial digital video systems
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The authors discuss ideas for evaluating serial digital interconnects. This includes error rates; signal levels; signal rise time; jitter; system return loss; and receiver dynamic range. They look at signal processing hardware, coax cables and connectors. Finally they give results of tests on an experimental system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aliasing effect on CCD professional TV cameras
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Advances in semiconductor technology mean that the broadcast quality charge-coupled device (CCD) television camera can compete with the TV tube camera. Although a CCD sensor is an analog device, it needs digital circuits to drive discrete charges to the output registers and transfer the optical picture into an electrical video signal. Through this development the professional CCD television camera has high sensitivity, better noise suppression, a better signal to noise ratio, better dynamic resolution good spectral response and less aliasing. The authors discuss resolution, camera response, signal-to-noise ratio, sensitivity and aliasing effects measured on the professional television cameras JVC KY 25 with Fujinon lenses and 728(H) x 587(V) CCD interline sensors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new noise meter for TV signals with the ability to discriminate noise components
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The noise generated by a solid-state imager contains two components, random noise and fixed pattern noise (FPN). The authors propose a way of discriminating between FPN and random noise. Based on that method and using digital technology, a new noise meter has been developed which is available for both the HDTV and NTSC systems by switching the clock frequency. The new noise meter is also capable of picking out flicker noise, horizontal (H) clamping noise and striped pattern noise from the whole noise signal. The noise spectrum analyzing function is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Methods for alignment of the colour balance of a TV monitor
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The authors describe the design of a colour analyser based on the CIE Standard Observed tristimulus system. It uses a trireceptor system consisting of three filters and three light-sensor-diodes. They describe how to use the analyser in xy-mode and RGB mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using digital signal processing in video measurements
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Applying DSP techniques to video system measurements offers a number of distinct advantages. One key advantage is that most measurements can be automated, allowing a button to be pushed for direct display or logging of measurement results. Another key advantage is that a wide range of measurement procedures can be condensed to DSP algorithms and integrated into a single instrument. The author looks at: video signal acquisition; measurements automation; noise spectrum measurement; intermodulation distortion (IMD) measurement; and chrominance AM/PM noise measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic measurement equipment for D2MAC/Packet signal
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Since the earliest days of television, broadcasting authorities have needed to check and assess the overall performance of the transmission chain. With MAC/Packet signals, this monitoring requires the use of new test signals and methods. The measurement equipment described has been used to validate the new monitoring method. The authors describe the prototype CCETT measurement equipment. Then they deal with the measurement methods, including the results obtained with the prototype.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital picture analyser for compatible HDMAC transmission chain
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The authors describe measurement equipment which was developed in the framework of the HDTV European project EUREKA-95. They first present the architecture of the HDTV chain so as to point out the digital interfaces where measurements can be taken. Then they describe the implementation of the measurement equipment and its performance. Finally they deal with some practical measurements which have been carried out on the EUREKA chain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance and acceptance testing of CCIR Rec. 601 based equipment
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: The authors describe their experiences in testing those digital component video systems that are defined in CCIR Rec. 601 and Rec. 656. The measurements are based on the technical information of EBU. The measurements include: signal paths; signal levels; frequency response; ADC linearity; and signal timing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent developments in picture quality evaluation
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: Image quality and impairment evaluation methods continue to develop in the light of experience, and to respond to the demands of new systems. The author outlines some recent progress in procedures, and particular developments associated with digital system evaluation and HDTV evaluation. The needs of digital television may be met by a new concept termed the 'picture-content failure-characteristics'. The needs of HDTV evaluations include new viewing conditions. Furthermore, a recent challenge in HDTV was to compare the quality potential of alternative HDTV production standards. He explains how a real scene was used as a reference in this case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic measurement of TV camera performance and colorimetry in the studio and control room
publicationTitle: Fourth International Conference on Television Measurements 1991
abstract: There are many parameters peculiar to cameras which require special test patterns for them to be measured. These test patterns often vary between broadcasters so it would be difficult to arrive at a standard. Also, full automation is not possible because of the need to physically place test patterns in front of the camera so that the whole transducer including lens, optical splitter and electronics can be tested. Measurements on cameras are particularly time consuming and therefore not cost effective. This situation invites automation and the author has designed the basis of a system which goes some way in solving the problem. He describes this system for automatic measurement of television camera performance. He also describes additions which have been made so that colorimetry measurements can also be carried out.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
